summary: This informational document provides a model of the information needed by the Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) process in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs). The model supports computing optical paths that obey constraints.

plainLanguage.summary: Choosing a path through an optical network means checking both the route and which wavelengths each piece of equipment can use. This RFC lists the information a path calculation needs.

questions: information model for optical path computation
what is routing and wavelength assignment
what is a connectivity matrix in optical networks
subtitle: The information needed to compute constrained paths through wavelength-switched optical networks.

tldr.problem: A wavelength-switched optical network must choose a route and a wavelength that satisfy the constraints of its links and equipment.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC models node, link, dynamic-node, and dynamic-link information for Routing and Wavelength Assignment calculations.
tldr.outcome: This Informational RFC defines an information model, not a protocol encoding. It does not model optical impairments.

today: RFC 7446 is an Informational document published in February 2015. The batch metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Information Model Supports
sections.content:
The model supports constrained optical path computation in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs). The Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) problem often includes wavelength continuity: a path must meet wavelength restrictions along its route.

The model captures compatibility constraints between signal attributes and network elements. It does not include constraints caused by optical impairments, and it is not a general-purpose network management model.
sections.plainLanguage: A path planner needs to know which wavelengths can pass through each link and device. This model supplies that information, but it does not assess every physical effect on an optical signal.

sections.title: Four Types of Information
sections.content:
The model has four categories: Node Information, Link Information, Dynamic Node Information, and Dynamic Link Information. It separates relatively static details, such as port connectivity, from details that change as connections are established or removed.

Keeping changing information separate can allow it to be updated without redistributing the larger set of relatively static information. The RFC uses Routing Backus-Naur Form (RBNF) to describe the model's structure.
sections.plainLanguage: Some network facts change rarely, while available wavelengths and resource use can change with connections. The model puts these types of information in separate categories.

sections.title: Node Connectivity and Resources
sections.content:
General node information includes an identifier and one or more connectivity matrices. Each matrix describes which input ports can potentially connect to which output ports; it does not describe internal blocking that depends on the device's current state.

WSON-specific information describes limited resources such as regenerators and wavelength converters. A resource pool groups similar resource blocks and can describe which inputs can reach them, how many resources are in use, and which outputs they can reach.
sections.plainLanguage: The model records which ports may connect and which limited optical resources can be reached. It can also record how many resources in a pool are in use.

sections.title: Link Properties and Wavelength Restrictions
sections.content:
Link information can include administrative groups, switching capabilities, protection, shared-risk link groups, traffic-engineering metrics, and port label restrictions. A shared-risk link group identifies links that may fail together.

Port label restrictions describe which wavelengths a port may use, how many channels it can carry, or whether a wavelength may be used only once across a set of ports. These details help the path computation avoid incompatible choices.
sections.plainLanguage: The model records link properties that affect route choice, including which wavelengths a port can carry. It can also identify links that may fail together.

sections.title: Information That Changes During Operation
sections.content:
Dynamic link information includes the wavelengths currently available and, when needed, wavelengths used for shared backup protection. Dynamic node information currently covers the state of a resource pool.

The RFC does not specify how this information must be encoded or where it must appear in a routing protocol. Those details depend on the protocol extensions that carry the information.
sections.plainLanguage: The changing information includes which wavelengths are free and how many pooled resources are in use. This RFC leaves the wire encoding to other protocol specifications.
